what: slot-geometry controls for the depth-3 variant slice
rule: the depth-3 verdict for slots/shrink is a GEOMETRY ARTIFACT if the same n_slots change reproduces the depth-3 deficit at depth 2 (control a) and/or the deficit disappears at width 192 where 6x32 is exact (control b).

a_depth2_geometry_slots.label: CONTROL A - slots at depth 2 width 128: 8x16 vs the published 4x32. Same depth, same width, same parameters; only the slot geometry moves. If 8x16 costs induction HERE, the depth-3 slots deficit is not evidence about the architecture.

a_depth2_geometry_shrink.label: CONTROL A - shrink at depth 2 width 128: 8x16 vs the published 4x32.

b_width192_slots_vs_plain.label: CONTROL B - depth 3 width 192, where 6 slots x 32 is EXACT: slots against the plain model at the same width. This is the depth-3 verdict re-run with the geometry the architecture wants.

b_width192_shrink_vs_plain.label: CONTROL B - shrink against plain at depth 3 width 192.

b2_width192_geometry_only.label: CONTROL B2 - the geometry contrast at FIXED width 192: 8x24 (two dead slots) against 6x32. Isolates slot geometry from width.

w128_slots_vs_plain.label: REFERENCE - the depth-3 width-128 comparison the verdict was read from (slots 8x16 vs plain).

w128_shrink_vs_plain.label: REFERENCE - shrink 8x16 vs plain at depth 3 width 128.

indicative_rule_with_masked_arms_at_thei.caveat: MIXES TWO WIDTHS - the three small-decoder arms are read at width 128 against the plain model at width 128, the two masked-decoder arms at width 192 against the plain model at width 192. It is not the registered rule and must never be quoted as it; it answers only "could the forced geometry alone have flipped the verdict word?"
